signals.detail: 8 distinct design tells: cream-palette, reflex-font-2, hero-then-proof, icon-tile-stack, italic-serif-display, pill-everything, icon-tile-grid, hero-eyebrow-chip
score 0.05, not typical of what Claude builds for this brief

actions.what: Write art-direction.json: run craft direction init, then give every choice a reason from the client's world.

Pick the display face from the client's world (signage, packaging, the trade's lettering) and record why in art-direction.json. If this face really is the right one, declare an exception with the reason and the evidence.
actions.why: Second-wave reflex font (reflex-font-2, gen 2), in source and on the page; Italic serif display (italic-serif-display, gen 2), in source and on the page

actions.what: Take the ground from the client's material world (paper stock, wall colour, tile). If it really is cream, say why.
actions.why: Cream ground (cream-palette, gen 2), in source and on the page

actions.what: Choose the shape language on purpose (and record it), then use the pill only where it means something. The limit here is 30 per scan.
actions.why: Pills everywhere (pill-everything, gen 1), in source and on the page

actions.what: Follow the hero with the thing only this business has: the work, the place, the person. Put proof where a doubt arises.
actions.why: Hero straight into a trust strip (hero-then-proof, gen 1), in source and on the page

actions.what: Show the services as the client would: a price list, a menu board, photographs of the work, a sequence.
actions.why: Three-column icon-card grid (icon-tile-grid, gen 1), in source and on the page

actions.what: Use the client's own marks, photography or numerals. If an icon earns its place, set it inline with the text.
actions.why: Icon in a tinted tile (icon-tile-stack, gen 2)

actions.what: Drop it. If the fact matters, put it in the headline or the first line of copy.
actions.why: Eyebrow chip above the hero (hero-eyebrow-chip, gen 2)
Rhetorical question opener (rhetorical-opener), 1 place, first at app/guides/[slug]/page.tsx:249

actions.what: Use a full stop, a comma, or a colon. Two sentences are clearer than one sentence with a dash in it.
actions.why: Em dash (em-dash), 24 places, first at components/sections/ServicesInline.tsx:33

actions.what: Say what is actually true. 'World-class service' becomes 'We answer the phone until 8pm'. 'Reach out' becomes 'get in touch'.
Say what they get: 'The price on the quote is the price you pay', 'Cancel any month'.
actions.why: Negative reassurance (negative-reassurance), 3 places, first at lib/locations.ts:90

actions.what: Keep the one that lands hardest and cut the rest. 'What is genuinely excellent' reads better as 'what is excellent'.
actions.why: Review-tier phrase (review-phrase), 6 places, first at lib/locations.ts:445

actions.what: Replace it with the positive fact it hints at, or cut it.
actions.why: 'No X' badge (no-x-badge), 10 places, first at lib/sanity/get-homepage-content.ts:211

actions.what: Remove it. Typographic marks are fine: a star for a rating, a middot as a separator, an arrow in a link.
actions.why: Emoji in copy (emoji), 10 places, first at public/social-media-kit/CHEAT-SHEET.txt:118

actions.what: Write one sentence that says which of the three is true, and how you know.
actions.why: Staccato triplet (staccato-triplet), 2 places, first at reels/src/BrandOutro.tsx:68

actions.what: Say what they get: 'We reply within a day and only about your enquiry'.
actions.why: 'No X, no Y' list (no-x-no-y), 1 place, first at reels/src/data/carousels.ts:92

actions.what: Say what the place is and where it is.
actions.why: 'Where X meets Y' (where-x-meets-y), 1 place, first at scripts/create-minor-works-guides.ts:355
